problem: Existing VLN surveys mostly organize work by task, dataset or technique and lack a unified view of how agent cognitive capability progresses, especially with the rise of foundation models.
motivation: VLN is central to embodied AI, and the shift from reactive policies to LLM-based reasoning agents needs a coherent framework. Piaget's developmental stages are used to map the technical progression from basic perception-action coupling to abstract reasoning.
key_idea: Categorize VLN research into four Piagetian cognitive stages (Sensorimotor, Preoperational, Concrete Operational, Formal Operational) to trace the evolution from reactive to abstract-reasoning agents.
insight: Only the abstract was available. It claims that foundation models accelerate the transition between stages, and that grounding language models in embodied environments and bridging perception with high-level cognition are the key open challenges. No ablations or experiments are reported, as this is a survey.
method: Sensorimotor stage: basic perception-action coupling, reactive behaviors
Preoperational stage: symbolic processing and memory
Formal Operational stage: abstract reasoning, driven by foundation models
Challenges and suggestions: grounding language models in embodied environments and bridging perception with high-level cognition
numbers_note: abstract only; survey with no experiments
results: A survey with no quantitative results. It contributes a four-stage cognitive-developmental taxonomy of VLN agents and highlights the accelerating role of foundation models.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details of coverage are unknown
Piagetian analogy is a conceptual framing that may not map cleanly onto technical methods
